key_insight: Picard–Chebyshev weakly nonlinear analysis predicts streak-breakdown triggers by tracking how streak–planar-wave interactions generate oblique waves and harmonics.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support transition prediction in channel flows by identifying finite-amplitude disturbances capable of triggering turbulence.
method: Formulate weakly nonlinear optimal perturbation analysis for compressible parallel flows using Picard–Chebyshev iteration.
Track non-modal amplification and nonlinear interactions across an expanding set of wavenumber components.
Recover linear dynamics at first order and weakly nonlinear amplitude dynamics at third order, with further iterations approaching DNS.
evidence_signal: For subcritical plane Poiseuille flow at Mach 0.3 and Reynolds number 3000, the abstract reports high agreement with DNS and identifies an optimal planar-wave perturbation that triggers streak breakdown in full nonlinear simulation.
watch_item: Demonstrated accuracy is limited to the reported flow conditions and weakly nonlinear regime; broader applicability requires validation.
paper_title: Predicting trigger in streak breakdown via Picard-Chebyshev approach in plane-Poiseuille flow
